def is_prime(num):
    if num < 2:
        return False
    for i in range(2, int(num ** 0.5) + 1):
        if num % i == 0:
            return False
    return True

def count_up_to(n):
    """Implement a function that takes an non-negative integer and returns an array of the first n
    integers that are prime numbers and less than n.
    
    Note: Based on your examples, it seems you want all primes strictly less than n,
    not "the first n primes". The docstring description matches the examples when interpreted as:
    "return all prime numbers < n"
    """
    if n <= 2:
        return []
    
    primes = [p for p in range(2, n) if is_prime(p)]
    return primes

# Examples:
print(count_up_to(5))   # [2, 3]
print(count_up_to(11))  # [2, 3, 5, 7]
print(count_up_to(0))   # []
print(count_up_to(20))  # [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19]
print(count_up_to(1))   # []
print(count_up_to(18))  # [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17]

            return False

    "return all prime numbers < n"
    """
    if n <= 2:
        return []
    
    primes = [p for p in range(2, n) if is_prime(p)]
    return primes

# Examples:
print(count_up_to(5))   # [2, 3]
print(count_up_to(11))  # [2, 3, 5, 7]
